questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available for exchange students at host university as well as economic possibilities to live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was overall quite easy. My host university provided lengthy emails with all information needed to know where to go and what to do the first couple of days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Offline introduction event. Visa and residence and mandatory healthcare insurance being handled through a third party company for a relatively small fee.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: South Korea had a complicated bureaucratic Visa system leading to a lot of time spent on completing their tasks.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of possibilities in the city of Seoul, however as all big metropolis scamming and unfortunate arrangements is common over the internet. I would recommend either finding a english speaking real estate agent specialising in foreigners or wait with sending deposits/rent for ones housing until you have arrived in Seoul. There facebook groups and other local possibilities is possible by meeting the potential landlord before agreeing to a contract

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Seoul is a big city with a very good public transport network making it easy and possible to live further away from your university than you'd expect. However, living off campus is usually much more expensive than on the dorms and often includes a quite big deposit that can be hard to get back if you dont have a korean bank account.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
After succesfull application, you would receive your account to their internal platform where registration happend in 3 rounds. 
First round is by milage/points "bidding" on which courses you would want. The more points you bid on one course the higher the chances you would get that course. This could be very hard to know which courses is popular and thus hard to get into, as you cannot easily find the bidding results from last year. 

If you did not get the courses you bidded for then in the second round you could register for remaining spaces in other courses by a first come first serve basis. 

Last round were the last possible opportunity to get into a course and would only happend by contacting the respective professor  and getting a signature on a special application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much if you do not know anyone who has attended the university before. There is a discord server for Yonsei University with alumnis that can answer your questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the first round i actually got 4 out of the 5 courses i wanted. However, later i found out one of my courses was unavailable for exchange students leading to me needing to find two whole new courses in the second round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Check the courses you want how much available space there is and allocate your points accordingly. I.e. if there is only 20 spaces use more points. 

Korean Language courses are extremely competitive so allocate a lot of points
 
Have some backup courses so you dont need to find new courses between the first and second phase of registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses where the level was harder and/or more extensive than what i had tried before at UCPH (which was the local level 4 courses). I had one course (local level 3) that was similar to and a bit easier compared to UCPH. My last course (local level 2) was much easier compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more focus on rote learning compared to UCPH and the detail level was a bit less however there was a lot more topics to cover. Syllabus was much more extensive than UCPH courses of the same ETCS level, but as said level of detail a bit less.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cancer Biology
Functional Genomics
Neuroscience: Exploring the Brain
Virus and Host
Introduction to AI and its application

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cancer Biology - An amazing professor with good english and teaching skills. Overall a very well planned course. Giant recommendation!! Molecular biology or signal transduction or similar courses is needed as a requisite otherwise it will be a hard course.

Functional Genomics - It is a very very hard course with a LOT of material on the syllabus, however if you are interested in 'Omics you get a really good foundation of all the different methods for 'Omics work. Microbiology/biology/general chemistry or similar is required as a requisite. 

Virus and Host - a overall good course focusing on virology and virus-related immunology. A good introduction to both topics if you have not had a lot of experience in these topics. However some biology / medicinal requisite is needed.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Mandatory healthcare insurance and a subscription to a company helping you with your visa application (residence card issue) after arriving 
A lot of housing fees
Furniture not provided at most rental. For me it was luckily only a duvet/pillow and all kitchen items

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food in supermarkeds are more expensive then i expected however eating at resturants is much less expensive.
Public transport is 7.5 DKK pr trip no matter the distance/time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Multiple sports days both for viewing and participating
Social Clubs
Introduction and farewell parties
Mentor/mentee partnerships both 1-1 and in a group
Paid social/langauge courses and events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The group mentor programs allows you to meet a 20-25 other exchange students leading to easy friendsships.
Introduction party is practically just a night out in a bar, however it allows you to maybe meet some new friends.
Sports days and other paid events are high quality and allows you to have some fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take on trips arranged by local temples or foreign tour arrangers. The tours made by Simple Spaces is really a recommendation, however you need to know someone that lives at their facilities to participate or ask them at their bar in HBC.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy in some situations and hard in others. There are a lot of cultural and social norms when in public and when greeting Koreans. Please remember to study this to really increase your chance of good interactions

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: At the university a lot of local students keep to themselves as it is a place of study. Here they do not really want to talk to you. However at events,, clubs, bars, mentor groups, social clubs they are as easy to talk to as everyone. I would recommend meeting them here

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of really weird legal complicated rules with apartment rental. Please find an english-speaking agent to help you. The trash sorting system is complicated and sometimes requires a bit of Korean to buy the correct trash bags as they are not displayed in any stores, you can either ask your landlord or the internet how to ask for them in stores. 

A lot of places only take local credit cards so cash is a must. Your public transport card is only available to purchase with cash

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The vibes of the city of Seoul at all times is great, safe and foreigner accessible. You would really get to experience the Korean Culture especially if you can say a few Korean words as they instantly like you just by you saying Hi and thank you in Korean. 

It has amazing hiking and nature possibilities closeby which is a recommendation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Extensive research in course selection
Try all the different local restaurants in your area
Be organised in your insurance and visa application. Keep all important documents on paper and digital for it to be much smoother.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Most danish insurance is good enough to qualify for exemption of the mandatory health insurance of Korea leading to a good amount of money saved.
Convenience stores are the place to go for garbage bags, transportation cards and a cheap meal.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting local students and receiving their help to study as a korean. 
Experience the many different parts of Seoul as each district is different and can provide you with new experiences 
The many beautiful hiking places

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my deposit back from my landlord as he was not that great at english and could only transfer it to a korean bank account which i did not own. Therefore my earlier comments on housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
